title: Fixed ordinary-to-derived Hom comparison on a ringed site
statement: Let (C,J,R) be a small ringed site with independent universes and its unbounded derived category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix the ordinary internal Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex], the functorial K-injective resolution and its augmentation eta [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and the fixed derived-Hom representative comparison [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. Define c(E,F): Q Hom(E,F) to RHom(QE,QF) by localizing Hom(id_E,eta_F) and composing with the inverse fixed representative comparison. If Hom(id_E,eta_F) is a quasi-isomorphism, c(E,F) is an isomorphism. This is the same augmentation, chain-map action, comparison morphism and comparison isomorphism used in the coefficient-duality normalization; no new choice is made.

source.place: Tags 079P, 0A8X and 0A95: fixed K-injective augmentation, ordinary Hom bifunctor, and comparison with derived Hom.

proof.text: The fixed representative comparison is already an isomorphism. Localization inverts the assumed quasi-isomorphism Hom(id_E,eta_F). Hence the displayed composite of these two isomorphisms is an isomorphism. All definitions and the proof are moved verbatim from the coefficient-duality module; this separates the comparison from shift and restriction compatibility without changing any object or morphism. The argument applies to zero and unbounded complexes, arbitrary characteristics and all recorded universes.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0A95; factor the comparison as the localized augmentation followed by the inverse fixed representative comparison.
